audit_amendment.reason: The first completed geometry computation showed that total-convergence maxima usually begin inside the frozen 20 kpc baryon-arrival radius, making the peak backtrack length nearly zero. This is a valid overlap observation but not a useful test of an apparent diffuse dark component.
audit_amendment.preserved_primary: The full-field tensor feasibility, minimum anisotropy, uncertainty, and method-control definitions are unchanged.
audit_amendment.added_diagnostic: Weight the same field-alignment test and select backtrack starting peaks using the positive residual after subtracting the non-negative least-squares projection of the normalized local baryon-light map from the normalized lensing map.
audit_amendment.selection_limit: The residual diagnostic is descriptive and cannot alter the predeclared full-field gates.

question: Can the apparent cluster gravity field inferred from standard lensing maps be interpreted as a locally redirected, conserved field sourced only by baryonic matter, and from which baryonic structures would its high-convergence locations backtrack?

field_ansatz.positivity: K is symmetric positive definite so it redirects and rescales a field without locally reversing its energy-sign analogue
field_ansatz.apparent_dark_component: rho_app-rho_b is proportional to div[(I-K)*g_L]; it is a response-divergence pattern, not a material source
field_ansatz.local_existence_test: A positive-definite K mapping g_L to J_b exists at a pixel if and only if dot(g_L,J_b)>0
field_ansatz.minimum_anisotropy: chi_min=(1+abs(sin(theta)))/(1-abs(sin(theta))), where theta is the angle between g_L and J_b
field_ansatz.scope: This stage measures the pointwise lower bound. It does not yet solve a globally smooth K or a covariant four-dimensional completion.

data.holdout_caveat: The holdout is untouched by P0567 model selection but is globally spent because earlier gravity-arc experiments inspected it.
data.baryon_proxy: strict photometric member positions weighted by positive F160W flux
data.lensing_method_control: GLAFIC best convergence map where locally available
data.model_dependence: Every convergence map is a standard-GR parametric reconstruction and can contain member-galaxy priors; it is an assumed apparent-mass location map, not a raw observation.

preprocessing.lensing_positive_residual: subtract finite 250-300 kpc annular median, clip at zero, smooth, and normalize
preprocessing.poisson_boundary: zero-pad each compact source map to twice its linear size before FFT inversion

backtracking.peak_target: positive residual after subtracting the non-negative least-squares projection of the normalized baryon-light map from normalized convergence
backtracking.rule: Start at each high-residual apparent-dark peak and integrate along the baryon-flux direction until it reaches a catalogued baryonic member or leaves the analysis domain.
backtracking.interpretation: These paths are source attributions under the baryonic field, not observed three-dimensional trajectories.

predeclared_diagnostics.local_feasibility_gate: pooled convergence-weighted feasible fraction at least 0.90 and every fresh system at least 0.75
predeclared_diagnostics.practical_distortion_gate: pooled feasible-pixel median chi_min at most 4 and 90th percentile at most 20
predeclared_diagnostics.method_robustness_gate: median absolute Lenstool-versus-GLAFIC feasible-fraction difference at most 0.10
predeclared_diagnostics.no_promotion: Passing establishes only that a local tensor representation is geometrically possible; it does not establish a predictive law or remove dark matter.

claim_limits: F160W member light omits hot gas, intracluster light, and stellar mass-to-light variation, so failure can diagnose an inadequate baryon map rather than the field ansatz alone.
The lensing convergence targets are model products, not direct measurements and not independent of standard-GR assumptions.
A two-dimensional map cannot determine whether a route bends in the lens plane, along the line of sight, or through an additional field dimension.
Pointwise K is underdetermined. The reported chi_min is only the least anisotropy any local positive tensor would require.
Absolute gravity strength is deliberately factored out in this morphology test.
A useful theory must later compress K into a universal baryon-only law and predict raw image positions, shear, time delays, galaxy dynamics, and Solar-system nulls.
